answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and slash that stake when peers prove duplicate identities. Like a tide that tests every hull at the wharf, the market checks work history before trusting a newcomer, so a faker standing on the ledge of entry must pay real collateral for every copy. Creating ten thousand fake agents then costs ten thousand stakes, while honest agents keep one deposit and earn fees, making mass forgery unprofitable.
